rows.title: While many small-town newspapers are vanishing, these Coloradans are working to keep local news alive
rows.standfirst: As many outlets scramble to publish following the closure of a key Colorado press, determined communities look at all options to preserve their voices

rows.title: New condos are hard to find in Colorado. Getting developers to build more will roil the Capitol next year.
rows.standfirst: Construction defects liability has been politically fraught, but the failure of Gov. Jared Polis’ signature land-use measure has reignited the push for lawmakers to take on the issue

rows.title: More Colorado energy co-ops line up to leave Xcel, Tri-State for cleaner, cheaper electricity providers
rows.standfirst: United Power will be the next to go, with 7 other smaller co-ops attempting to renegotiate contracts or find price stability on their own

rows.title: Monarch Mountain plans new terrain as visitation, pass sales soar
rows.standfirst: The expansion plan at Monarch ski area is the first in nearly 20 years for a resort seeking Forest Service approval to expand beyond its special-use permit boundary

rows.title: The Newton experiment: How a rural Kansas weekly newspaper refreshed an outdated business model
rows.standfirst: When researchers sought to refresh a stale business model for rural weekly newspapers, they looked for a fearless innovator to thest their findings. Now they’re hoping they can export his success to other small papers, including in Colorado.

rows.title: An old-fashioned newspaper war inspired by modern politics is raging in Westcliffe and dividing readers
rows.standfirst: While many Colorado communities are losing their local newspapers, Custer County readers are divided between a traditional, 100-year-old paper and a right-wing newcomer

rows.title: Opera Colorado workers cleared to vote on unionization
rows.standfirst: National Labor Relations Board rules Denver opera company performers and stage staff are eligible for a collective bargaining unit. They will vote on forming a union starting Oct. 16.

rows.title: What we learned from Colorado’s governor — including his position on some hot-button issues — at SunFest
rows.standfirst: Jared Polis talked about everything from affordable housing to passenger rail to water conservation when he appeared at the inaugural Colorado Sun festival convening the state’s civic and cultural leaders

rows.title: Colorado Supreme Court to hear case against Christian baker who refused to make cake celebrating gender transition
rows.standfirst: Jack Phillips won a partial victory before the U.S. Supreme Court in 2018 after refusing to make a gay couple’s wedding cake

rows.title: Thousands of Kaiser Permanente workers go on strike in Colorado, other states over wages and staff shortages
rows.standfirst: The Coalition of Kaiser Permanente Unions, representing about 85,000 of the health system’s employees nationally, approved a strike for three days

rows.title: Denver International Airport adding 100 more gates by 2045 to accommodate double the passengers served today
rows.standfirst: The country’s third-busiest airport has plans for four new walkable concourses to help handle an increasing number of travelers, officials said

rows.title: Colorado rancher loses bid to raise $198,000 fine against oil company that poisoned his cows
rows.standfirst: Cattle consumed oil that spilled from a well operated by Western Operating. K&T Cattle argued the fine to settle that and three other violations was too low.

rows.title: How does Colorado solve its homelessness problem? Here are three programs that could help.
rows.standfirst: One doles out cash payments, another allows renters to build credit by paying on time, and a third trains people to work as live-in maintenance workers

rows.title: Kaiser Permanente strike in Colorado, other states heads into final day with no deal in sight
rows.standfirst: Kaiser spokesperson Hilary Costa said the company was working to reconvene bargaining “as soon as possible.”

rows.title: Federal electric vehicle tax credit change will turbocharge Colorado sales, local officials say
rows.standfirst: Electric vehicle buyers next year can get $7,500 in federal credit off the top at time of purchase, in addition to state rebates and other incentives.

rows.title: Affordable housing goes 3D with efforts focused on building a hub in Greeley
rows.standfirst: Alquist 3D, which is partnering with Habitat for Humanity on 100 3D-printed homes, is also teaming up with Aims Community College on a 3D-printing workforce program.

rows.title: What’s Working: What Colorado’s population will look like in the future
rows.standfirst: State Demographer Elizabeth Garner talks about migration and answers questions leftover from SunFest. Plus: Affordable housing experiments, Kaiser strike updates, more!

rows.title: Telluride readies $857 per-bedroom “regulatory fee” on short-term rentals as replacement for moratorium
rows.standfirst: Three other Colorado communities charge annual per-bedroom fees for short-term rentals as more than a dozen other communities have increased license fees or passed excise taxes

rows.title: Proposition HH: What you need to know about the Colorado property tax relief plan
rows.standfirst: The measure would limit the increase in Colorado property owners’ taxes, but it would also have big effects on state and local budgets and reduce Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights refunds over time

rows.title: A Colorado county’s creative effort to provide property tax relief could lead to a showdown with the state
rows.standfirst: Douglas County’s Republican commissioners reduced residential property values by 4%. A state board controlled by Democrats may try to roll back the decision.

rows.title: Colorado’s radon mitigation assistance program has become more popular
rows.standfirst: About one in every two tests conducted statewide show radon levels exceed EPA health limits. Radon kills more than 500 annually in Colorado.

rows.title: Kaiser Permanente reaches tentative deal with health care worker unions after recent strike
rows.standfirst: There are 3,000 Colorado health care workers in the union, and the president of the local union calls the agreement “historic.”

rows.title: What’s Working: Didn’t know Colorado is a leader in clean energy and quantum? A Tech Hub designation could change that.
rows.standfirst: Results are imminent for feds picking 20 innovation hubs. But is it just a marketing tool? Plus: Denver inflation up to 5.4%, Comcast picks Colorado Springs for tech rollout and more!

rows.title: Sale of Ouray silver mine leaves creditors owed $60 million in the cold
rows.standfirst: OURAY — The recent $1.8 million sale of a historic silver mine above Ouray will leave its creditors — who collectively are owed upward of $60 million — almost entirely out in the cold with no clear path to recouping their losses. The Revenue-Virginius Mine in Yankee Boy Basin was auctioned off in early August […]

rows.title: A homeless recovery campus at an old fort on the plains is so successful Colorado is making more
rows.standfirst: Fort Lyon, a serene campus amid the farmland of southeastern Colorado, has been home to more than 2,200 people over the past decade

rows.title: Colorado has robust laws against human trafficking — but it’s hardly using them
rows.standfirst: A new report says the state needs to strengthen its trafficking task forces and include more people who reflect local communities, including immigrants

rows.title: Skiing in Windsor? Where there’s water — and snowmaking equipment — there’s a way
rows.standfirst: Water Valley neighborhood developers say the public Hoedown Hill, with its 130-foot drop, fits right in with the golf course and water park amenities on the south side of the Larimer County town

rows.title: Fact check: Would Proposition HH really eliminate Coloradans’ taxpayer refunds?
rows.standfirst: The measure increases the chance that the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights cap won’t be exceeded in a given year, which would block refunds from going out, but it wouldn’t outright halt them permanently

rows.title: No, Proposition HH doesn’t raise property taxes. But it’s unlikely to cut them as much as supporters say.
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun fact-checked misleading claims made by both sides on the 2023 Colorado ballot measure

rows.title: Cable industry pushes next generation of cable tech, with Colorado leading the way
rows.standfirst: Industry leaders converged in Denver for the cable technology event. But most didn’t travel too far since many are based in Colorado.

rows.title: Distilleries taking a shot on Colorado’s mountain towns are finding lots of success
rows.standfirst: The small-scale liquor-makers are also becoming rural economic engines for these towns, providing jobs, tax revenues and a valuable attraction for visitors

rows.title: Colorado named U.S. Tech Hub for quantum computing
rows.standfirst: The designation comes with federal funding, bragging rights as the next big tech ecosystem, and local excitement to make the state the Silicon Valley of quantum technology.

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s unemployment rate has risen to 3.2%. Here’s why that’s “not significant”
rows.standfirst: There’s a growing number of unemployed Coloradans but officials say the rate is similar to the pre-pandemic era. Plus: The cable industry returns to Denver but really the industry never left.

rows.title: Colorado passes mandate for 82% electric vehicle sales by 2032
rows.standfirst: Environmental groups wanted an extension to 100% EVs by 2035, but officials declare the state on track as EV sales hit 17% last quarter.

rows.title: “Super-emitting” oil wells near Denver are releasing 142% more pollution per hour than state average, CSU study finds
rows.standfirst: Adams County had three wells with massive emissions, the largest leaking 165 pounds of methane per hour. State will use the data to prioritize plugging orphan wells.

rows.title: Colorado, 32 other states sue Meta claiming its social platforms are addictive and harm children’s mental health
rows.standfirst: A lawsuit filed by 33 states in federal court in California, claims that Meta routinely collects data on children under 13 without their parents’ consent

rows.title: Creative districts designed to boost rural Colorado’s economy creatively tackle other problems, too
rows.standfirst: Now 30 communities in distressed urban and rural areas of Colorado are certified as Creative Districts, which helps boost tourism and creative programs, and sometimes housing.

rows.title: Former owner of Granby Ranch smuggled gems, is hiding assets in shell companies, lawsuit claims
rows.standfirst: Marise Cipriani’s sister claims the former developer has offered to repay a $19 million loan with “several million dollars worth of uncut gems” while her son faces diamond smuggling charges in Florida.

rows.title: Colorado judge chastises company that tried to pay $23,500 settlement with loose change
rows.standfirst: Instead of writing a check, a welding company sent its payment via 3 tons of coins, which one attorney called a “symbolic middle finger.”

rows.title: Propuesta HH: Lo que necesita saber acerca del plan de ayuda fiscal sobre bienes inmuebles en Colorado
rows.standfirst: La Propuesta HH mitigaría esos elevados impuestos inmobiliarios en Colorado al menos por los siguientes 10 años. También haría crecer el presupuesto estatal, pondría nuevos límites al gasto de los gobiernos locales y modificaría la forma en que se distribuyen los reembolsos a los contribuyentes.

rows.title: CORE Energy awarded $26.5M in compensation for prolonged shutdowns of Xcel-run power plant in Pueblo
rows.standfirst: Xcel and CORE say the fight over which company is responsible for fixing the troubled Comanche 3 plant and the cost of buying power on the open market isn’t done

rows.title: How Boulder became a hub for quantum technology
rows.standfirst: Before Colorado was named a quantum Tech Hub, an ecosystem existed with roots dating back to the 1950s. Now, a push to commercialize quantum.

rows.title: K.P. Kauffman faces big bond bill as Colorado regulators find $133 million is needed to properly close 1,089 wells
rows.standfirst: The company, which has already sued the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, says it will fight this commission ruling, too

rows.title: What’s Working: The number of open jobs in Colorado is a sign the labor market may be stabilizing
rows.standfirst: At least that’s the business community’s take on new job-openings data. Plus: Wage growth is flat, if not lower when adjusted for inflation.

rows.title: PHOTOS: Colorado onion harvesting races against freezing weather
rows.standfirst: Colorado is one of the largest producers of onions in the U.S. Western Slope growers are moving fast to make sure millions of pounds of red, yellow and white varieties are out of the ground in time for the holidays.

rows.title: How extreme weather in Colorado and other states may have affected the pumpkins you picked this year for Halloween
rows.standfirst: Pumpkins can survive hot, dry weather to an extent, but this summer’s heat, which broke world records, was just too much
